title: Trini Callaloo
subtitle: Trinidadian braised callaloo leaves with coconut milk and okra
excerpt: Callaloo leaves, okra, and coconut milk cooked together until silky and thick. The traditional Trinidadian Sunday dish, eaten alongside rice and peas or macaroni pie.
sourceNotes: Trinidadian callaloo tradition. The okra acts as a thickener alongside the coconut milk. This vegetarian version omits crab or pig tail used in some traditional versions.

recipe.freezeNotes: Callaloo freezes well. Cool completely and freeze in portions. Reheat gently on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the recipe easily. It reheats well and improves the next day.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day ahead and refrigerate. The flavour deepens overnight.

content.text: Callaloo is blended at the end to give it its characteristic smooth texture. The okra adds natural body without any starch. Use spinach if callaloo leaves are not available, though the flavour will be milder.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and spring onion and cook for 1 minute more.
Add the okra and stir to coat. Cook for 3 minutes until slightly softened.
Add the callaloo leaves in batches, stirring each batch down before adding the next. They will reduce dramatically.
Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable stock. Add the thyme sprigs and the whole scotch bonnet. Season with salt. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over a low heat for 20 to 25 minutes until everything is very soft. Remove the scotch bonnet and thyme sprigs.
Use a stick blender to blend the callaloo in the pot until smooth and silky. For a thinner consistency, add a splash of water and blend again. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve hot.

items.cause: The okra released a lot of natural thickener during cooking.
items.fix: Add water or vegetable stock a little at a time after blending until you reach a pourable consistency.

items.cause: The scotch bonnet split or was left in too long.
items.fix: Use the scotch bonnet whole next time and remove it after 15 minutes of simmering. Leaving it whole rather than cutting it gives much milder heat.

items.cause: Insufficient salt or the stock was too weak.
items.fix: Season generously. Callaloo needs more salt than you might expect because of the large volume of leaves.
